rows.notes: Immediate strict read of the same Editable predicate as Strider actions and expectations: enabled, not read-only, and a text/settable input, textarea or contenteditable element. rows.notes: Immediate strict read of the same Editable predicate as Strider actions and expectations: enabled, not read-only, and a text/settable input, textarea or contenteditable element. Unsupported kinds return false, including selects, checkboxes and ARIA-only textboxes; Playwright accepts more kinds and throws for unsupported elements. Native readOnly and the element’s exact aria-readonly="true" prevent editing; aria-disabled="true" on any ancestor disables it. Hidden/inert elements may read true. NoMatch and StrictViolation fail immediately; no attachment wait. Uses the existing owned read path, including frame targets, access release and operation deadlines. Contenteditable follows native isContentEditable; WebKit may report false for hidden or inert contenteditable elements.

rows.notes: Immediate strict read of the same Editable predicate as Strider actions and expectations: enabled, not read-only, and a text/settable input, textarea or contenteditable element. Unsupported kinds return false, including selects, checkboxes and ARIA-only textboxes; Playwright accepts more kinds and throws for unsupported elements. Native readOnly and the element’s exact aria-readonly="true" prevent editing; aria-disabled="true" on any ancestor disables it. Hidden/inert elements may read true. NoMatch and StrictViolation fail immediately; no attachment wait. Uses the existing owned read path, including frame targets, access release and operation deadlines. Contenteditable follows native isContentEditable; WebKit may report false for hidden or inert contenteditable elements.

 * uninterruptible work or finalizers.

rows.notes: Cancel the running operation by interrupting its fiber (Fiber.interrupt waits for cleanup); no per-call AbortSignal parameter. Deadline.within separately bounds operation time with a typed timeout; a deadline is not a cancellation signal. Parent-operation browser limits still apply.

visible: Expect.toBeVisible; hidden: Expect.toBeHidden (also succeeds for no matches). Use locator.first for non-strict selector visible/hidden waits, and the full locator for strict waits. attached: Expect.toHaveCount(1) on locator.first; detached: Expect.toHaveCount(0) on the full locator. These expectations retry until the condition holds; Locator.count alone is an immediate read, not a wait. For a strict single-match attached wait, use toHaveCount(1) on the full locator, but it retries multiple matches instead of immediately throwing Playwright strict-mode errors. Hidden/count expectations also do not reproduce every strict-mode failure. Non-strict selector waits can select the first match; disappearance waits require zero matches, not merely a hidden first match. Compositions return no retained ElementHandle: lazy locators re-resolve, so fixed element/subtree identity and handle-return semantics are not provided.

rows.notes: Cancel the running operation by interrupting its fiber (Fiber.interrupt waits for cleanup); no per-call AbortSignal parameter. visible: Expect.toBeVisible; hidden: Expect.toBeHidden (also succeeds for no matches). Use locator.first for non-strict selector visible/hidden waits, and the full locator for strict waits. attached: Expect.toHaveCount(1) on locator.first; detached: Expect.toHaveCount(0) on the full locator. These expectations retry until the condition holds; Locator.count alone is an immediate read, not a wait. For a strict single-match attached wait, use toHaveCount(1) on the full locator, but it retries multiple matches instead of immediately throwing Playwright strict-mode errors. Hidden/count expectations also do not reproduce every strict-mode failure. Non-strict selector waits can select the first match; disappearance waits require zero matches, not merely a hidden first match. Compositions return no retained ElementHandle: lazy locators re-resolve, so fixed element/subtree identity and handle-return semantics are not provided.

audit.scope: Pinned params.md wait-for-selector-state and class-locator.md waitFor compared with engine Visible, Hidden and Count expectations. Count expectations provide presence/absence waits; no exact strict-error or retained-handle equivalence is claimed.

source.quote:
Interruption is cooperative. A fiber can continue running while it is inside
 * uninterruptible work or finalizers.

rows.notes: Cancel the running operation by interrupting its fiber (Fiber.interrupt waits for cleanup); no per-call AbortSignal parameter. Interruption is cooperative: uninterruptible work and finalizers may delay completion. It produces Effect interruption rather than an AbortSignal error and does not undo browser side effects or commands already sent. Deadline.within separately bounds operation time with a typed timeout; a deadline is not a cancellation signal. Parent-operation browser limits still apply.

visible: Expect.toBeVisible; hidden: Expect.toBeHidden (also succeeds for no matches). Use locator.first for non-strict selector visible/hidden waits, and the full locator for strict waits. attached: Expect.toHaveCount(1) on locator.first; detached: Expect.toHaveCount(0) on the full locator. These expectations retry until the condition holds; Locator.count alone is an immediate read, not a wait. For a strict single-match attached wait, use toHaveCount(1) on the full locator, but it retries multiple matches instead of immediately throwing Playwright strict-mode errors. Hidden/count expectations also do not reproduce every strict-mode failure. Non-strict selector waits can select the first match; disappearance waits require zero matches, not merely a hidden first match. Compositions return no retained ElementHandle: lazy locators re-resolve, so fixed element/subtree identity and handle-return semantics are not provided.

audit.scope: Pinned params.md wait-for-selector-state and class-locator.md waitFor compared with engine Visible, Hidden and Count expectations. Count expectations provide presence/absence waits; no exact strict-error or retained-handle equivalence is claimed.

visible: Expect.toBeVisible; hidden: Expect.toBeHidden (also succeeds for no matches). Use locator.first for non-strict selector visible/hidden waits, and the full locator for strict waits. attached: Expect.toHaveCount(1) on locator.first; detached: Expect.toHaveCount(0) on the full locator. These expectations retry until the condition holds; Locator.count alone is an immediate read, not a wait. For a strict single-match attached wait, use toHaveCount(1) on the full locator, but it retries multiple matches instead of immediately throwing Playwright strict-mode errors. Hidden/count expectations also do not reproduce every strict-mode failure. Non-strict selector waits can select the first match; disappearance waits require zero matches, not merely a hidden first match. Compositions return no retained ElementHandle: lazy locators re-resolve, so fixed element/subtree identity and handle-return semantics are not provided.

audit.scope: Pinned params.md wait-for-selector-state and class-locator.md waitFor compared with engine Visible, Hidden and Count expectations. Count expectations provide presence/absence waits; no exact strict-error or retained-handle equivalence is claimed.

source.quote:
Interruption is cooperative. A fiber can continue running while it is inside
 * uninterruptible work or finalizers.

rows.notes: Cancel the running operation by interrupting its fiber (Fiber.interrupt waits for cleanup); no per-call AbortSignal parameter. Interruption is cooperative: uninterruptible work and finalizers may delay completion. It produces Effect interruption rather than an AbortSignal error and does not undo browser side effects or commands already sent. Deadline.within separately bounds operation time with a typed timeout; a deadline is not a cancellation signal. Parent-operation browser limits still apply.

scopeDecisions.title: Android and Electron automation
scopeDecisions.note: Separate device and application platforms are outside the 1.0 browser target.

scopeDecisions.title: Playwright server-wire compatibility
scopeDecisions.note: Strider speaks browser protocols directly. Playwright's server protocol is private and changes between releases, so compatibility with it isn't planned at any milestone.

scopeDecisions.title: Interactive debugger, recorder and inspection toolchain
scopeDecisions.note: Not part of the library. A graphical debugger, recorder or inspection overlay may come later as a separate package; until then the CLI's snapshots and `strider export test` cover recording a session as a test.

scopeDecisions.title: WebMCP-specific APIs
scopeDecisions.note: Not a separate API. If the WebMCP proposal settles, the agent toolkit would offer the tools a page registers beside its own browser tools.

scopeDecisions.title: A duplicate assertion and runner framework
scopeDecisions.note: Duplicating generic assertions or an entire runner/reporter framework is outside 1.0. Optional Playwright Test integration and the existing Vitest integration remain the integration path; browser-specific assertions and visual baselines are not excluded.
